title: Mushroom Spinach Egg Toasts
description: Savory toast topped with quick sautéed mushrooms, spinach, and soft scrambled eggs.
substitutions: Use frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry.

steps.text: Scramble in eggs and spoon over toast.

cookSteps.text: Toast 4 slices bread to your liking.
Heat 1 tablespoon butter or oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook 1 cup sliced mushrooms for about 4 minutes until browned.
Add 1 cup spinach and stir about 1 minute until wilted.
Beat 4 eggs with 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Pour them into the skillet and gently scramble 2–3 minutes until softly set.
Divide the mushroom-spinach eggs over the 4 toast slices.

storage: Best fresh; refrigerate egg mixture up to 2 days.

title: Creamy White Bean & Pea Pasta
description: A creamy-feeling pantry pasta made from mashed white beans, peas, and pasta water instead of a heavy sauce.
substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans, mashing them well.
Skip parmesan and add an extra spoonful of olive oil for a dairy-free version.

steps.text: Cook pasta and reserve some pasta water.
Mash beans into a rough sauce.
Toss pasta, peas, beans, and seasonings together.

cookSteps.text: Cook 8 ounces short pasta in salted water according to the package. Before draining, save 1 cup pasta water.
Return the pot to low heat. Add 1 can white beans, 1 tablespoon olive oil or butter, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Mash about half the beans with a fork.
Add 1 cup frozen peas, the drained pasta, and 1/2 cup reserved pasta water. Stir 2–3 minutes until hot and creamy, adding more pasta water if needed.
Stir in 1/2 cup parmesan if using and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; loosen with a splash of water when reheating.

title: Honey Mustard Cabbage Slaw
description: Crunchy cabbage tossed with a simple sweet-tangy dressing that works beside sandwiches, potatoes, or beans.

ingredients.item: apple cider vinegar or lemon juice

substitutions: Use bagged coleslaw mix for the cabbage and carrot.
Use maple syrup instead of honey.

steps.text: Serve right away or chill briefly.

cookSteps.text: Whisk 2 tablespoons mayonnaise or yogurt, 1 tablespoon mustard, 1 tablespoon honey, 1 tablespoon vinegar or lemon juice, and 1/4 teaspoon salt in a large bowl.
Add 5 cups sliced cabbage and 1 grated carrot if using. Toss until evenly coated.
Serve now for maximum crunch, or refrigerate 15–30 minutes for a softer slaw.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. It softens as it sits but remains good for sandwiches and bowls.

title: Baked Apple French Toast Cups
description: Individual baked French-toast cups that use up bread and an apple for an easy breakfast or snack.

ingredients.item: bread cubes, preferably a little stale

substitutions: Use a pear instead of apple.
Use any sturdy sandwich bread, brioche, or leftover rolls.

steps.text: Heat oven and grease muffin cups.
Fill cups and bake until set.

cookSteps.text: Heat oven to 350°F and grease 6 muffin cups well.
Whisk 3 eggs, 1 cup milk, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla if using.
Fold in 4 cups bread cubes and 1 diced apple. Let sit 5 minutes so the bread absorbs some custard.
Divide the mixture among the 6 muffin cups and press gently.
Bake 22–25 minutes until puffed and set in the centers.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat briefly in the microwave or toaster oven.
